about.content:
{imagem} nome: fabio-sales-about.png tamanho: PP classes: var(--shadow-2) borda: 50% {} h1: I design clarity inside complex systems For three decades, I have worked across visual design, product, technology, and business — leading multidisciplinary teams, creating systems, and staying close to the craft. My career did not move from design to technology. It expanded from designing information to designing the systems, interactions, and software through which people experience it. {faixa} pasta: faixa-about tempo: 100 imagem_1: atbl-login.jpg | Sign-in screen of the ATBL shipping app imagem_2: anatomia.jpg | “A anatomia do novo Estadão”, 2021 imagem_3: estadao-2010.jpg | Election section opener, Estadão, 2010 imagem_4: atbl-conferencia.jpg | Order checking in the ATBL shipping app imagem_5: discursos.jpg | Inaugural speeches graphic, Estadão imagem_6: correio-2001.jpg | “De joelhos”, Correio Braziliense, 2001 imagem_7: novo-estadao.jpg | Special section presenting the new Estadão, 2021 imagem_8: correio-2002.jpg | “Enfim, lá!”, Correio Braziliense, 2002 imagem_9: atbl-estoque.jpg | Stock put-away in the ATBL products app imagem_10: odia-ataque.jpg | Ataque cover, O Dia, 2000 {} h3: Craft is where it started Visual journalism taught me to make unfamiliar, dense information understandable under real constraints and real deadlines. At Estadão, Diário de Notícias, Correio Braziliense, and through international consulting, I worked across typography, information architecture, data visualization, art direction, interaction, and storytelling — while leading teams responsible for products used by large audiences. That work earned hundreds of national and international distinctions. More importantly, it taught me that craft scales only when it becomes a shared system rather than the intuition of a few individuals. h3: Leadership means building the conditions for good work I believe a design leader has two responsibilities at the same time: raise the quality bar and build an environment in which teams can reach it repeatedly. That means creating principles and reusable systems, giving clear direction without prescribing every answer, connecting design decisions to business and technology, and remaining close enough to the work to recognize when the details are not good enough yet. h3: Technology extended the design surface Since 2010, I have increasingly worked with software as part of the design process. Today I build with JavaScript, Svelte, React, Python, SQL, APIs, ERP integrations, and AI-assisted workflows. I do not see engineering as a second career. It gives me another way to prototype ideas, understand constraints, collaborate with technical teams, and take product decisions all the way to production. h3: Today At ATBL, I work at the intersection of product, operations, technology, and business transformation. The problems are very different from a newsroom, but the design challenge is familiar: complex rules, fragmented information, specialist knowledge, and users who should not have to understand the infrastructure underneath the experience. Understand complexity deeply enough to make the experience feel simple. {divisor} {capitulos} titulo: Selected career chapters capitulo_1: ATBL | 2025–Present | Transformation and Innovation leadership. Product strategy, digital operations, ERP integration, AI workflows, and hands-on product development. imagem_1: capitulos/atbl-telas.png legenda_1: Delivery routes, the workshop panel, and stock put-away in the ATBL apps. capitulo_2: Independent | 2023–2025 | Product, technology, and business-process consulting; full-stack development and automation. capitulo_3: Estadão | 2005–2023 | Executive Art Editor. Led visual culture, redesign, information design, digital experimentation, and multidisciplinary creative teams. imagem_3: capitulos/estadao-2010.jpg papel_3: sim legenda_3: Opening page of the election section, October 4, 2010: the result told as one running text. capitulo_4: Diário de Notícias, Portugal | 2003–2005 | Consultant and Art Director. Led a redesign recognized by SND-e as Best Designed Newspaper in Iberia. imagem_4: capitulos/dn-estrada.jpg legenda_4: “Estrada mata 1390 pessoas”, a spread on road deaths in 2003, Diário de Notícias. papel_4: sim capitulo_5: Correio Braziliense | 2000–2003 | Art editor, then head of the art department. Front pages built on one strong image and one headline. imagem_5: capitulos/correio-2001.jpg legenda_5: “De joelhos”: a page from the edition of September 12, 2001. papel_5: sim capitulo_6: O Dia and O Globo | 1997–2000 | Designer, later deputy art editor. blue_case.content: {imagem} nome: blue/tablet.png tamanho: G alt: The Blue prototype on a tablet, with the section bar across the top and a story below tags: Product Design, UX/UI, Interaction Design {} h1: Blue — Designing for a New Interaction Model Consumer interaction / Touch interfaces / Information architecture / R&D Blue was created in 2010, when the tablet was still an emerging consumer platform. Rather than treat the device as a smaller desktop, the project asked: what changes when people navigate information primarily with their hands? h3: The context Financial news is continuous, dense, and time-sensitive. A touch device introduced different constraints from desktop: direct manipulation, changing orientation, less visible navigation chrome, and a stronger relationship between gesture and spatial movement. h3: The interaction hypothesis We explored gesture-based navigation and card-like structures for moving through the news stream. The goal was to create a spatial model people could understand through touch rather than reproduce the desktop interface. h3: Designing before the pattern library existed Today cards, swipes, touch targets, and responsive information blocks are ordinary vocabulary. At the time those conventions were still being negotiated. Blue was R&D as much as interface design: prototype, understand the medium, and establish useful patterns rather than wait for mature conventions to copy. h3: Why it still matters The visual language belongs to 2010. The product question does not: understand the capabilities and constraints of the platform, then design behavior around people rather than around the previous technology. ← Back to selected work

estadao.content:
imagem: germanico.png, G h1: Estadão — Designing a System at Scale Design leadership / Information architecture / Visual systems / Organizational change A newspaper redesign can look like a graphic-design exercise. The real challenge was systemic: evolve a daily information product while balancing readers, editorial priorities, industrial production, advertising, digital workflows, and business performance. {numeros} numero_1: 18 | Years at the paper, from 2005 to 2023 numero_2: R$7 million | Estimated EBITDA increase in 2022, according to the business case numero_3: 3 | Fronts the redesign had to serve at once: editorial, production, and advertising {} h3: A high-frequency interface before we called it product design Every day the content changes completely. The interface cannot. Readers need to recognize hierarchy and scan dense information in seconds; editors need flexibility without rebuilding the language every morning. Create enough consistency to make the product intuitive, and enough flexibility to keep it expressive. {imagem} nome: estadao/novo-estadao-capa.jpg tamanho: GG legenda: The special section that presented the new Estadão to readers, October 17, 2021. {} h3: My role — direction and craft I led the redesign strategy across art direction, information architecture, editorial leadership, production constraints, and commercial viability, while remaining close to typography, hierarchy, grids, modules, data visualization, and visual storytelling. {imagem} nome: estadao/novo-estadao-pesquisa.jpg tamanho: GG legenda: Reader research behind the new format, published in the same special section. {} h3: From pages to reusable decisions The system established reusable principles for typography, hierarchy, modular layouts, recurring patterns, and visual language — boundaries within which teams could make good decisions. Explore the redesign and design system →
Explore interactive & multimedia UI components → {imagem} nome: estadao/anatomia.jpg tamanho: GG legenda: “A anatomia do novo Estadão”, October 17, 2021. The spread explained the new format, sections, and typography to readers. {} h3: Craft and business The redesign supported production optimization and a new advertising strategy; its business case estimated a R$7 million increase in EBITDA in 2022. atbl.content: {celular} pasta: atbl entrada: login.jpg entrada_alt: Sign-in screen of the ATBL shipping app alt: A phone showing the ATBL sign-in screen, with three app screens sliding out beside it tela_1: exp-02.jpg | The day's orders tela_2: ofi-14.jpg | Hose assembly tela_3: prod-06.jpg | Stock put-away {} h1: ATBL — Turning Enterprise Complexity into a Usable Product A commercial transaction sits on top of specifications, inventory, customer pricing, taxes, approvals, ERP processes, documentation, and relationships. The design question was which complexity users need to see — and which complexity the system should absorb for them. h3: Product principles Show information needed to act, not infrastructure. Pricing, inventory, taxes, agreements, and status must reflect operational systems. Data already known by the ERP should not be reconstructed manually. Self-service handles routine information; technical salespeople focus on complex work. h3: The system behind the experience {sistema} titulo_cima: What people see visivel_1: Customer | A technical need and a commercial context. visivel_2: Portal and apps | Catalogue, stock, price, documents, and order status, on one screen. visivel_3: Delivery | Tracking and proof of delivery come back to the same place. titulo_baixo: What the system absorbs oculto_1: Inventory | by location, live from the ERP oculto_2: Customer pricing | agreements and price tables oculto_3: Taxes | calculated per order oculto_4: Approvals | credit and commercial rules oculto_5: Billing | the approved order, without retyping oculto_6: Records | what the app wrote, and when nota: Show what a decision needs. Absorb the rest. {} Complexity stays behind the experience. Customer-facing journeys connect to live operational data across portal, ERP, billing, and delivery. h3: Designing for technical B2B More than 26,000 active products require structured images, dimensions, attributes, standards, and technical metadata before an interface can make them meaningfully searchable. I designed and built products integrated with Sankhya ERP, keeping product decisions grounded in real inventory, pricing, and operational rules. Eight screens from the shipping, workshop, and stock apps, as they are used today. {telas} pasta: atbl imagem_1: exp-02.jpg chapeu_1: Shipping titulo_1: The day's orders on one screen texto_1: How many orders are waiting, checked, labelled, and out for delivery. The shipping team opens the day here. imagem_2: exp-03.jpg chapeu_2: Shipping titulo_2: Checking against the order texto_2: Each item is scanned against the order from the ERP. A difference shows up before the box is closed, not at the customer. imagem_3: exp-05.jpg chapeu_3: Shipping titulo_3: The route, stop by stop texto_3: Deliveries are grouped by driver, with distance, time on the road, and the order of the stops. imagem_4: exp-10.jpg chapeu_4: Shipping titulo_4: Proof of delivery, photographed texto_4: The driver photographs the signed receipt, and it goes back to the ERP attached to the invoice. imagem_5: ofi-01.jpg chapeu_5: Workshop titulo_5: What the hose workshop produced texto_5: Pieces assembled and inspected, approval rate, and assembly time, by day, week, or month. imagem_6: ofi-14.jpg chapeu_6: Workshop titulo_6: Assembly, measured texto_6: The assembler records each crimping measurement against the tolerance. The app times the job without anyone pressing a stopwatch. imagem_7: ofi-19.jpg chapeu_7: Workshop titulo_7: The certificate, straight from the assembly texto_7: The test certificate is generated from what was recorded during assembly and inspection, ready to print. imagem_8: prod-06.jpg chapeu_8: Stock titulo_8: Every product has an address texto_8: On arrival, each item is scanned to a shelf position. The location is written to the product record. {} h3: From interface to operating model Digital channels handle first-level service, stock and price checks, and order tracking; technical salespeople remain focused on engineering solutions and strategic negotiations. The company recorded a 12.5% revenue increase alongside these operational changes; I treat that as business context, not as a claim that interface design alone caused growth. h3: What is running today {numeros} numero_1: 6,359 | Deliveries recorded since July 2024 numero_2: 97% | Of confirmed deliveries have the proof of delivery attached numero_3: 9,269 | Hoses completed in the workshop since February 2025 numero_4: 99.9% | Of inspected hoses with a satisfactory result numero_5: 26,484 | Active products in the catalogue numero_6: 84% | Of the products sold online have a photo nota: Company records, as of October 13, 2026. {} Order checking, label printing, delivery routes, and proof of delivery, on the phones of the shipping team and the drivers. Hydraulic-hose assembly, from the order to inspection and the test certificate. Counter sales, stock movements, and product records with photos. The apps share one design system and the same foundations, and they read from and write to the ERP. h3: What this work demonstrates My role spans product judgment, information architecture, business rules, interaction decisions, technical implementation, and organizational adoption. Understand complexity deeply enough to make the experience feel simple. ← Back to selected work

newsletters.content: {imagem} nome: newsletters/saiba-agora.jpg tamanho: P {} h1: Personalized Newsletters — Testing Relevance at Scale Product experimentation / Editorial relevance / Cross-functional collaboration A daily newsletter gives every reader the same editorial selection. This experiment asked whether recommendations based on reading behavior could make that selection more relevant — and whether the evidence would justify changing the product. h3: My contribution I was part of the cross-functional Estadão team behind the InovaBra newsletter experiment, alongside colleagues from editorial, commercial, digital strategy, reader revenue, and technology. The work brought editorial judgment, recommendation systems, and audience measurement into the same product discussion. h3: An experiment inside an existing habit The test used Saiba Agora, an established subscriber briefing. Beluga and Itera each created five audience clusters using browsing history and two months of news coverage. Each partner recommended four stories per cluster. From December 10 to 16, the team sent eleven newsletter versions: five for each partner and one editorial control. Keeping the existing newsletter as a reference made it possible to compare personalization with the experience readers already knew. {numeros} numero_1: 11 | Newsletter versions sent: five for each partner and one editorial control numero_2: 10 | Audience clusters, five built by each partner numero_3: 4 | Stories recommended to each cluster numero_4: 7 | Days of testing, December 10 to 16 {} h3: Relevance needed more than a click The evaluation combined click-through rates on recommended stories, bounce rate, and reading time with a qualitative review of the editorial selections. Audience groups behaved differently, and the largest clusters strongly influenced the averages. {imagem} nome: newsletters/resultados.jpg tamanho: G {} h3: What the results actually showed Click-through results were close across Beluga, Itera, and Estadão. Some smaller clusters performed better, but the short test did not establish a clear overall uplift. Both partners showed lower bounce rates; reading time was higher for the existing Estadão selection. The useful signal was more specific: Beluga’s audience groups were more distinct, and its daily recommendations showed stronger affinity with those groups. Delivery processes and clarity of collaboration also mattered when assessing the next step. h3: The decision was another test The report recommended a further 30-day round with Beluga, ten refined clusters, and better automated measurement. That was a proposed next phase, not evidence of a completed rollout or a proven long-term gain. h3: What this work demonstrates Personalization is a product hypothesis that needs editorial and behavioral evidence. A responsible experiment makes the comparison explicit, exposes uncertainty, and turns mixed results into a better next decision. ← Back to selected work
